title: John Milton: Darkness Visible
dek: The blind poet who dictated Paradise Lost after sight failed.
mortality_event: Became totally blind by about 1652, then dictated Paradise Lost and other late works.

sources.name: Academy of American Poets — John Milton

citation_passage: John Milton (1608–1674) was an English poet and political writer who continued his literary work after losing his sight. His life spanned the English Civil War, the Commonwealth, and the Restoration, and his public writing included arguments about freedom of the press. By the early 1650s he was blind, but he continued working with assistance. Paradise Lost, first published in 1667, tells of Satan, Adam and Eve, and the loss of Eden in blank verse. Paradise Regained and Samson Agonistes followed in 1671. This eight-page biographical comic centers on blindness and the sustained work of composition, placing the late poems within a life shaped by political upheaval and personal loss.
